_source.orbits: JPL/Standish approximate elements, ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/planets/approx_pos.html Table 1 (1800-2050). Heliocentric, mean ecliptic and equinox of J2000. Table 1 needs no b/c/s/f correction terms; those apply only to Table 2 (3000 BC - 3000 AD).
_source.poles: IAU WGCCRE 2015 report. ICRF right ascension/declination of the north pole, prime meridian angle W.
_source.moon: Astronomical Almanac low-precision lunar formulae. Verified against JPL Horizons over 2026-2050: median 0.10 deg, max 0.24 deg, and NOT cumulative (2038-2050 mean 0.104 deg vs 2026-2038 mean 0.086 deg).
_source.rings: Ring radii from the named ring boundaries; the span matches saturn_ring_alpha.png, whose alpha profile puts the Cassini Division at u=0.694 vs 0.691 predicted.
notes: peri is the LONGITUDE of perihelion (varpi = node + argument of perihelion).
mDot is the mean motion in deg/day = JPL Ldot (deg/century) / 36525. Named by analogy with wDot.
m0 is the mean anomaly at J2000 = JPL L - varpi, wrapped to [0,360).
Only M (via mDot) and W (via wDot) advance with time; a/e/i/node/peri are held at their J2000 values. In a fixed J2000 frame their secular rates are <=0.33 deg/century.
EARTH IS THE EARTH-MOON BARYCENTRE. The true Earth centre is r_EMB - 0.012150585 * r_moon_geocentric, i.e. up to 4671 km away (0.73 Earth radii).
The Moon series is referred to the mean equinox OF DATE. Subtract the precession polynomial (deg) from its longitude to reach J2000, or it drifts 0.014 deg/yr.
Moon series tuples are [cD, cM, cMp, cF, amplitude]; argument = cD*D + cM*M + cMp*Mp + cF*F. lon sums onto L. par is horizontal parallax in deg; r = parRadiusKm / sin(par).
Dropped as negligible: T-terms in pole ra/dec (<0.01 deg by 2050), Neptune sin N libration (<=0.5 deg), Moon pole libration (+-4 deg).
Ring radii are absolute km from the planet centre, independent of diam.
_source.spacecraft: Voyager 1/2 heliocentric state vectors at JD 2460310.5, from JPL Horizons (COMMAND -31/-32, CENTER 500@10, REF_PLANE FRAME, OUT_UNITS AU-D), retrieved 2026-08-24. ICRF EQUATORIAL, unlike the ecliptic planetary elements above; both craft coast in a straight line from here, so position and velocity are all the model needs.
_source.heliosphere: nose = the interstellar neutral helium inflow axis measured by Ulysses and IBEX, ecliptic (255.7, 5.1) J2000 converted to ICRF equatorial; this is the Sun's motion relative to the LOCAL INTERSTELLAR CLOUD at ~26 km/s, 86 deg from the direction of the Sun's galactic orbit and 52 deg from the solar apex. standoffAu = Voyager 1's heliopause crossing, 2012-08-25 at 121.6 AU; Voyager 2 crossed 2018-11-05 at 119.0 AU, 53 deg from the nose, so the upwind boundary is very nearly spherical. The tail's extent is NOT here: it is unsettled by a factor of 30 between the croissant and comet models, so the renderer chooses it.
